transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, thank you for seeing me. I hope it's okay that I'm here. I just... well, I guess what brings me in is that I've been feeling a little down lately. I mean, it's probably nothing major, but I just keep feeling like I'm ruining things for everybody? Like, I'm in this pipefitting apprenticeship, which is great, I'm really lucky to have it, but I just feel like a total fake. And I keep worrying that I'm letting my family down, and the younger apprentices, over these little mistakes. I know other people would probably just fix it and move on, so I feel silly even bringing it up. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been a few weeks, or has this been going on for months or even years?

Um, well... I guess it's been a little while. Maybe around nine months? Give or take. I really tried to just push through it and not make a big deal out of it, because I didn't want to be a burden to anyone. But, um... lately it's just gotten a bit harder to hide. Like, my work at the apprenticeship and some of my classes started slipping a little bit, which I feel awful about. I really hate letting people down, so I've been trying my best to fix it. I hope that's okay to admit. Does that answer your question alright?
Over these past nine months, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy?

Um, yeah... I guess so. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm just being lazy or anything. It's just... lately, I can walk right past my sketchbook, and I've been skipping volleyball, which I usually love. I even ignore the volunteer group texts, and I don't really feel much of anything about it. Those used to be the things that made me feel like myself, you know? But I'm sure I just need to try harder to get back into them. I really don't want to come across like I don't care about my commitments. Is it normal to feel like that when you're a bit down?
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living during this time?

Oh. Um... well, I definitely don't have some plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I promise. I would never want to put my family or the people at the shop through that. 

But... I guess, sometimes, like when I'm driving home after class, or when I'm just lying awake at night... I do get these thoughts. Just... that maybe it would be easier if I just didn't wake up tomorrow. 

It's really just a passing thing, though, I swear. I try to just push it out of my head as soon as it happens. I hope it's okay that I told you that, I really don't want to sound dramatic or like I'm complaining too much. Is it... is it normal to have thoughts like that when you're feeling down?
How often are you having these thoughts about not waking up, and how strong or intrusive do they feel when they occur?

Um... I guess they happen maybe a couple times a week? Mostly just when I'm really tired and alone with my thoughts. They aren't super strong, really. It's more like a quiet sigh in the back of my head, just a fleeting "what if." I can usually distract myself pretty quickly if I just put on a podcast or start thinking about what I need to do at work the next day. I really try not to let them stick around. I know I have a lot to be grateful for, and I don't want to dwell on things that sound so... ungrateful. I hope that makes sense. I'm not trying to make a big deal out of it, I promise.

Over the past few weeks, has your low mood made it hard to get through your daily responsibilities—like getting to work or completing basic tasks—or have you still been able to manage them, even if it's been difficult?

Um... I mean, I'm still showing up. I really try to push through, because I know how lucky I am to have this apprenticeship. I definitely don't want to seem like I'm slacking off. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it has been getting a little harder lately. My instructors at school and my foreman at the site... they've had to remind me a few times about some unfinished sketches, and I guess my work has been a bit slower than usual. 

I'm trying so hard to fix it, I promise. I just... I get so worried that I'm going to mess up this certification that I've worked so hard for. I really don't want them to think I'm not dedicated. Is it okay that I'm struggling with it a little bit right now? I'm going to do better, I swear.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately—such as trouble falling asleep, waking up frequently, or sleeping much more or less than usual?

Um... well, my sleep has been a little all over the place, I guess. I hope it's not because I'm doing something wrong with my routine. 

Like, for a while there, I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours a night, but I felt totally fine! I was showing up to the site and to class completely wired and ready to go. I actually got a lot done. But... lately, it's changed. Now I just kind of lie there and can't fall asleep, or I'll wake up way before my alarm goes off, and I just feel... so tired. Like I haven't rested at all. 

I'm trying to drink less coffee in the afternoons, so maybe that will fix it? I really don't want to sound like I'm whining about being tired, because I know everyone works hard and gets exhausted. Is it normal for sleep to just switch like that? I'm trying my best to get back on a good schedule, I promise.

During that time when you were only sleeping three or four hours but felt fine and got a lot done, did you also notice your mood being unusually upbeat, more talkative, or full of racing ideas, and about how many days did that stretch last?

Um... yeah, I guess I was. I hope I didn't come across as too intense to anyone. 

It lasted for a few weeks, actually. I felt... I don't know, almost *too* good? Like I was on top of the world, like all of Miami was just mine for the taking. I had so many ideas about how to do things better at the site, and I was talking a lot more than usual. 

But... um, I'm a little embarrassed to admit this... I also got kind of snappy? Like, if a coworker was moving too slow or didn't understand what I was trying to explain, I would just lose my patience way faster than I normally would. I'd snap at them, which really isn't like me at all. I know how important it is to be a good team player, and I always want to be polite. 

I've been trying really hard to watch my tone since then, I promise. Do you think that's okay? Like, maybe I was just stressed and over-caffeinated during that time? I really don't want you to think I'm a difficult person to work with.
